question: What is the primary biological purpose of inflammation in the human body?

options.A: To stop all metabolic activity in affected areas
options.B: To permanently increase local blood pressure
options.C: To destroy healthy host tissue and cells
options.D: To remove tissue injury causes and begin repair

explanation: Inflammation serves as a defense mechanism to clear harmful agents and heal damaged tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why can the inflammatory response sometimes cause damage to the host?

options.A: It permanently deactivates the immune system
options.B: It can be excessive or directed inappropriately
options.C: It completely stops blood flow to organs
options.D: It is always caused by malignant cell growth

explanation: Overactive or misdirected immune responses lead to collateral damage in healthy tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which white blood cell type dominates during acute inflammation?
explanation: Neutrophils are the primary and rapid responders in acute inflammatory reactions. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h2)

question: What pathological feature distinguishes chronic inflammation from acute inflammation?
explanation: Chronic inflammation involves long-term tissue remodeling, including fibrosis and new blood vessel formation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h2)

question: What physiological change directly causes rubor during acute inflammation?
explanation: Vasodilation increases blood volume in the microvasculature, leading to visible redness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h3)

question: Chemical mediators such as prostaglandins contribute directly to which cardinal sign?
explanation: Prostaglandins and bradykinins sensitize nerve endings, generating the sensation of pain at the injury site. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the movement of leukocytes toward the site of injury called?
explanation: Chemotaxis is the chemical-guided movement of white blood cells toward the source of injury. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why does increased vascular permeability occur early in acute inflammation?

options.A: To prevent white blood cells from leaving blood vessels
options.B: To allow protein-rich fluid to enter the interstitial tissue
options.C: To speed up systemic blood circulation through the heart
options.D: To permanently close damaged local capillary networks

explanation: Endothelial gaps allow plasma proteins and fluids to escape into tissues, creating the inflammatory exudate. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which organ produces acute-phase proteins like C-reactive protein during systemic inflammation?
explanation: The liver synthesizes and releases large amounts of acute-phase proteins when stimulated by inflammatory cytokines. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h5)

question: What lab finding is most commonly associated with an ongoing acute inflammatory response?
explanation: CRP rises sharply in the bloodstream during inflammatory states, making it a key diagnostic marker. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h5)

question: A patient with a localized leg wound develops a fever and elevated heart rate. What do these findings indicate?

options.A: The patient is experiencing normal resting physiology
options.B: The inflammatory process has completely resolved
options.C: The inflammation has remained strictly local
options.D: The local injury has triggered a systemic response

explanation: Fever and tachycardia reflect systemic involvement rather than isolated local changes. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which nursing action is most important when monitoring a limb with acute soft tissue inflammation?

options.A: Limiting all patient movement to prevent joint stiffness
options.B: Measuring extremity circumference to track changes in edema
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to stop inflammatory exudate production
options.D: Applying continuous direct heat to speed up cellular repair

explanation: Regular measurement provides objective data on whether swelling is worsening or improving. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary pharmacological action of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs?

options.A: Inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes to reduce prostaglandins
options.B: Increasing local blood flow to clear cellular debris
options.C: Stimulating the bone marrow to produce more neutrophils
options.D: Blocking all nerve transmission in the central nervous system

explanation: NSAIDs block the COX pathway, preventing the formation of pain-producing prostaglandins. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is cold therapy recommended during the first 24 to 48 hours after an acute soft tissue injury?

options.A: It triggers immediate vasodilation to bring more white blood cells
options.B: It permanently removes all damaged collagen fibers from the area
options.C: It increases local cellular metabolism to speed up tissue healing
options.D: It causes vasoconstriction to minimize local swelling and pain

explanation: Cold constricts local blood vessels, decreasing fluid leakage into tissues and numbing nerve endings. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is a primary long-term consequence of uncontrolled chronic inflammation in organs?

options.A: Continuous decrease in systemic blood pressure
options.C: Rapid regeneration of normal functional cells
options.D: Permanent cessation of local immune activity

explanation: Prolonged chronic inflammation leads to scarring and loss of normal tissue architecture. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h8)

question: Which instruction is most appropriate when educating a patient recovering from a localized infection?

options.A: Apply heat packs continuously to prevent any swelling
options.B: Ignore mild discomfort because it indicates healing
options.C: Watch for spreading redness, increased pain, or pus
options.D: Stop taking prescribed antibiotics once the fever drops

explanation: Patients must monitor for warning signs that indicate worsening infection or inflammation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h8)
